reason: A generic name for a tine of something forked (a thorn, style, stigma or apex). Like 'arm' and 'segment' in the 2026-11-13 review, it needs the organ it belongs to; the count is better read as a forked or divided quality of that organ.

A position adjective (on the commissure, the inner face where two mericarps meet), not a part. The part is the following noun: vitta (FLOPO_0986042) or vascular bundle (PO_0005020). Treat it like 'lateral' and 'basal' in the previous review.

A relative measure ('3/4 length of leaf'): the bearer is the part being described (petiole, sheath), and the leaf is only the thing it is compared with. 'fraction' was rejected as not a structure on 2026-11-13.

A 'per X' counting phrase; the counted part is the flower. Same as 'per node', 'per axil' and 'per cluster' in the previous review. Note: in these floras (Urticaceae, Amaranthaceae) a glomerule is a dense cluster of flowers, so the PO synonym on compound capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030122) would ground it wrongly.
Narrower in use: floras mean the stems and leaves as opposed to flowers and fruits (indumentum, farina, reduction), which is the vegetative shoot system. Roots are rarely meant.
Exact: 'female inflorescence' is a PO synonym of pistillate inflorescence. The miss probably comes from the plural or French forms.

PO gives 'barb' as a synonym of prickle, thorn, spine leaf and spine stipule. Here it mostly means the small backward-pointing teeth on pappus awns, bristles or spines. Generic: it needs the organ, and the quality is barbed (FLOPO:0991209) or retrorse on that organ.

label: pseudoparaphyllium
parent: is_a PO_0005679 (plant epidermis); part_of PO_0030020 (gametophore axis)
definition: A portion of plant epidermis (PO:0005679) that is a leaf-like or filamentous outgrowth surrounding a branch primordium on a gametophore axis (PO:0030020) of a pleurocarpous moss. Unlike paraphyllia (PO:0030069), it is confined to the region around branch primordia.
reason: A real moss structure, used in 4 floras and distinct from paraphyllium (PO:0030069). Modelled on the PO paraphyllium term; should be proposed to PO (Bryophytes subset).
Generic: the fertile joints of a Salicornia-type spike, of a fern frond, and so on. 'segment' and 'fertile' were both rejected on 2026-11-13; it needs the organ.
A lobe of the lemma apex: a region of an existing class, expressed with the lobe-of-whole pattern. The lemma is a phyllome.
Narrower: pappus scale is a synonym of pappus element. 'aristate' is a quality of the scale (awned), not part of the bearer name. All examples are pappus.

target: leaf lamina vein (PO_0020138), counted on one side of the midvein
reason: The bearer is the lateral veins (secondary leaf vein PO_0020140 when stated as lateral). 'per side' gives the count per half-lamina; a position in a series that the counting pattern can express.
A position in a whorl or series (inner sepals, inner bracts); the part is the noun it qualifies or the elided subject. Treat it like 'primary' and 'lateral' in the previous review.
A relative width ('1/6–1/3 the width of the leaves'); the leaf is only the thing compared with. See 'fraction'.
A quality: hyaline is a synonym of PATO_0000964 transparent. The part is the hairpoint, awn or appendage that follows.
Exact: 'sucker' is a PO synonym of root-borne shoot system ('suckers from roots'). Exclude the parasite sense ('suckers (haustoria)') and climbers' adhesive disks, which are other structures.

target: carpel (PO_0009030): an apical appendage of the carpel, using the part-of-whole pattern
reason: An outgrowth of the carpel (e.g. on the apical part of free carpels). Qualified by its whole, so it can be expressed as part of carpel without a new class.
The apex region of an existing class. Pinnule was grounded to FLOPO_0985028 in the previous review; leaflet apex (FLOPO_0986000) is the broader alternative.
A rank or size adjective (major veins, major lateral lobes); the part is the noun that follows. Treat it like 'primary' and 'secondary'.
Narrower: a false umbel is a contracted cyme that looks like an umbel, not a true umbel (PO_0030129).
Exact: the French for flower. With ♀/♂ it is pistillate (PO_0025599) or staminate flower.
A generic narrow connecting part (between leaf lobes, mericarps, fruit segments or anther halves); it needs the organ it belongs to.

label: gynobase
parent: is_a PO_0025001 (cardinal organ part); part_of PO_0009064 (receptacle)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is an enlarged, raised portion of the receptacle (PO:0009064), on which the lobes of a deeply lobed ovary sit and from whose base the style arises, as in Boraginaceae and Lamiaceae.
reason: A real floral structure that floras describe (flat, conic, lobed, fastigiate), with no PO class. Distinct from gynophore (PO_0006330), which is a stalk. Should be proposed to PO.
Same as 'lateral lobe', rejected on 2026-11-13: generic, it needs the organ (lip, corolla, leaf).

label: chlorocyst
parent: is_a PO_0009002 (plant cell); part_of PO_0025075 (non-vascular leaf)
definition: A plant cell (PO:0009002) that is a narrow, living, chlorophyll-containing cell of the leaf of Sphagnum, forming a network between the large dead hyaline cells (hyalocysts).
reason: A real cell type central to Sphagnum keys (its cross-section shape), used by 4 floras and not in PO. Propose to PO together with hyalocyst.

target: margin of indusium (FLOPO_0986020), using the margin-of-whole pattern
reason: The margin region of an existing FLOPO anatomy class.
Exact: lacuna/lacunae are PO synonyms of plant anatomical space (air spaces beside the midvein in leaves).

Small rounded teeth on whatever organ is described (petal or ligule apex, margin). Generic: it needs the organ. Only on a leaf is it leaf lamina crena (PO_0025519); otherwise read it as a crenulate quality of that organ.
A branching event or pattern ('1–3 times dichotomous'), i.e. the number of forkings of the rachis or axis. A quality of that axis, not a part.

target: bract (PO_0009055), outer members of the series
reason: A position in a series of an existing class. Use involucral bract (PO_0009045) when the context is an involucre.
